subject: Life Skills
atp_edition: undated (DBE Grade R Resource Kit 'Laying Solid Foundations for Learning')
basis: DBE Grade R Resource Kit lesson plans (no ATP published)

terms.theme: My body; My senses; My family; Keeping clean and fit; Healthy eating

topics.name: My body
subtopics: Names body parts and the actions the body can do; identifies basic rights and responsibilities
Looks at self in a mirror and describes self; assembles body puzzles and bodies from magazine cut-outs; 'Me book'
Creative Arts: body rubbings, traced body mural, playdough bodies, hand and foot prints, paper-plate faces, biscuit faces
Hand washing routine and rhymes; health check
Physical Education: hula hoops, ball throwing and catching, bean bag aiming and balancing; music ring (Hokey Pokey, body dice)

topics.name: My senses
subtopics: Names the five senses and how the body uses them to explore the world
Lists items experienced with each sense and items experienced with more than one sense
Science: explores popcorn with the senses; visual memory tray game; draws own face in detail from a mirror
Creative Arts: 'Things I like to hear' collage, shaving-foam and texture collages, nature collage, blow painting, paper-plate tambourines
Technology: bakes a fruit salad

topics.name: My family
subtopics: Names family members and describes each member's role in the family
What it means to be part of a family and how to look after the family
Guessing game with family members' clothing and accessories
Creative Arts: drawings of family at home, spoon and finger puppets, plasticine family, shades-of-green collage
Technology: makes fruit jelly; builds a 'family home' with blocks

topics.name: Keeping clean and fit
subtopics: How we keep our bodies clean; names cleaning products, what they are used for and on which body part
Steps for personal hygiene: correct tooth brushing (small tooth-brushing book)
Fun exercises to strengthen the body and get fit
Creative Arts: dental-floss art, ball art, mixing playdough colours, ear-bud painting; memory box game

topics.name: Healthy eating
subtopics: Makes healthy food choices; discusses food groups and how much to eat from each
Importance of drinking clean water and eating fresh food; sorts foods into two groups and explains
Science: grows cress in eggshells
Creative Arts and Technology: mielie-cob prints, peanut and macaroni necklaces, edible art, pizza-face baking, kitchen gadget painting

sba: Life skills assessment (weeks 1-2): from pictures, name body parts, the action and the body part used
Life skills assessment (weeks 3-4): name the five senses, list items per sense and explain experiences using more than one sense
Life skills assessment (weeks 5-6): from pictures, name family members and describe their roles
Life skills assessment (weeks 7-8): name cleaning products, their use and the body part they are used on
Life skills assessment (weeks 9-10): name foods and divide them into two groups with reasons

terms.theme: Friends; This is what I wear; Shapes and colours in my community; Opposites; Gardens and bugs

topics.name: Friends
subtopics: How to treat a friend, how to be a good friend and what to expect from a friend
Things friends do together; describes pictures of friends
Makes a friendship fruit salad; bakes heart-shaped biscuits and plaits a friendship bracelet to give a friend
Creative Arts: noodle designs, finger painting, chalk pictures, deodorant-bottle painting

topics.name: This is what I wear
subtopics: Names items of clothing and describes their function, who wears them and why
Season and occasion for which clothing is worn (winter/summer washing line, party outfits)
Materials used to make clothes; pairs shoes and discusses who wears them
Creative Arts and Technology: clothing mobiles, suitcase from a small box, fabric collage, party hats, paper-plate crowns, sock puppets

topics.name: Shapes and colours in my community
subtopics: Becomes aware of shapes and colours in the environment
Colour mixing: primary colours make secondary colours
Uses shapes to create pictures and patterns: marble painting, toothpick shapes, doily shape borders, shape stick puppets, shape prints
Bakes biscuits with shape cutters; visual discrimination memory game

topics.name: Opposites
subtopics: Names opposites for actions and objects
Explores ways of moving the body, including rotate, elevate and balance
Science: things that change from hard to soft or soft to hard (raw and boiled egg, pasta)
Creative Arts: bark rubbings, painting with hard and soft items, fat and thin string painting, big and small finger puppets

topics.name: Gardens and bugs
subtopics: Classifies insects (six legs) and spiders (eight legs); an insect's body has head, thorax and abdomen
Describes what insects look like, what they eat, where they live and whether they are dangerous
Parts of a plant
Creative Arts and Technology: potato bugs, painted rock insects, pressed-flower collage, blob-painted butterflies, spider prints, handprint bugs, bug stick-puppets

sba: Life skills assessment (weeks 11-12): describe pictures of pairs of friends and what they like to do with friends
Life skills assessment (weeks 13-14): name clothing, who wears it and why, the season and the occasion
Life skills assessment (weeks 15-16): name shapes and colours, describe shapes, identify primary colours and the colour made by mixing two
Life skills assessment (weeks 17-18): name pictures, match opposites and name other opposites
Life skills assessment (weeks 19-20): name and describe insects, what they eat, where they live and whether dangerous

terms.theme: Time and weather; Keeping safe; The sky (day and night); People who help us; Helping hands

topics.name: Time and weather
subtopics: Weather: how clouds fill with water and fall as rain (cotton-wool experiment); weather board
Works collaboratively and co-operatively to a set of classroom rules: listens to instructions, shares resources, ideas and space, waits for turn
Makes carrot salad; carrot-top and 'c'-shaped prints; bead necklaces

topics.name: Keeping safe
subtopics: Identifies safe and unsafe situations in the home, at school and in the environment
Fire as a help and a danger; how to put out a fire; potentially dangerous objects and cutlery
Safe and unsafe product labels (cleaning agents, medication, poisons); warning signs
Stranger danger; adults learners trust and strangers who help us (police, nurses)
Safety equipment: where, when and why it is used (sunglasses, hard hat, armbands); traffic lights
Science and Technology: smelling pots (the nose warns of danger); floating and sinking; safe use of kitchen tools

topics.name: The sky (day and night)
subtopics: Investigates and reflects on natural phenomena: what causes day and night (globe and torch)
Day and night sandwich; things seen in the sky by day and by night
Creative Arts: night collage with crepe paper and tinfoil, cut-out shapes projected with a torch through a tube, jewelled crescent crowns

topics.name: People who help us
subtopics: People who help us at home, at school and in the community: where they work, what they do and their special skills
How community workers help keep us safe and healthy
Science and Technology: fingerprints as clues (police work)
Creative Arts: garbage-bag prints on newspaper; plasticine pens and pencils; role play (police car)

topics.name: Helping hands
subtopics: How learners can help at home, at school and in the community
Recognises when people need help, shows empathy and suggests practical ways to help
Being young and old: ways to help elderly people; card of appreciation for grandparents
Ubuntu: making and sharing bread rolls (unbaked and baked dough)
Creative Arts: decorated 'charity' money boxes with plasticine coins

sba: Life skills assessment (weeks 21-22): observation checklist of co-operative behaviour (listens, participates, shares, waits for turn)
Life skills assessment (weeks 23-24): where, when and why safety items are used (sunglasses, hard hat, armbands)
Life skills assessment (weeks 25-26): observation checklist of investigating natural phenomena (interest, questions, observations)
Life skills assessment (weeks 27-28): from pictures, who the helper is, where they work and how they keep us safe/healthy
Life skills assessment (weeks 29-30): from pictures, why the person needs help, how they feel and how to help (observation)

terms.theme: New life; This is where people live

topics.name: New life
subtopics: Life cycle of a butterfly; baby animals and their mothers
Natural Sciences: describes animal skin, hair and fur by touch (smooth, furry, rough)
Uses the body to represent animals in nature: locomotor, rotation, elevation and balance movements; gross and fine motor co-ordination; crossing the mid-line
Creative Arts (Dance): expressive movement, changes in tempo, simple dances based on formations and patterns; paper blossoms on a cardboard tree

topics.name: This is where people live
subtopics: Different types of homes and what homes are made of; a home provides shelter and safety
Rooms in a home, their furnishings and household sounds (Poster 17); how a house is built in sequence
Buildings in the community (shop, clinic, school, post office) and why they are needed; learners' own addresses
Homes in the past (grandparents' stories); neighbourhood walk; home safety rules; animal homes compared with people's homes
Creative Arts and Technology: dip-and-dye patterns, stained-glass windows, homes from boxes, doodle patterns, exploring locks
Physical Education and music: dodge-ball, pretend builders, 'This is the way we build our house', movement to Carnival of the Animals

sba: Life skills assessment (weeks 31-32): observation of movement (locomote, rotate, elevate, balance), expressive movement and simple dances
